sub_scenario.family: rehearsal load versus protected voice clarity
sub_scenario.one_line: emergency management planner: accept the single rehearsal and decline the add-on run

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the incident map and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The exercise brief review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I handle a five-minute radio check at shift change.
That is much shorter than an exercise rehearsal.
And it does not require calling commands across the room.
Someone new shadowed me in the coordination room this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the storm season into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
On 18 February, I ran the flood-tabletop rehearsal after the command cards had been revised asynchronously by every agency.
What was the result the next day?
I gave the 08:00 public-safety briefing crisply because the rehearsal had one focused pass.
I can circulate a decision tree and collect edits in writing.
So the briefing can be prepared without extra speaking.
That is how I resolve most wording disputes.
I archived last cycle's notes on the exercise brief and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
You once facilitated a long afternoon workshop successfully.
Yes, but it followed two quiet days and there was no dawn briefing after it.
The calendar around the load was different.
A vendor call about the incident map ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the coordination room checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the storm season.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the exercise brief records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
On 29 May, an unplanned second rehearsal stretched until 20:30 before a 07:45 wildfire briefing.
What failed?
My voice cracked during the opening instructions and the deputy took the media questions.
I sketched next week's plan for the storm season before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the incident map updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
I am recovering from a respiratory infection, and my doctor asked me to avoid prolonged evening projection for another week.
Does that rule out all preparation?
No, just the kind that delays vocal recovery.
The mayor's office says the extended rehearsal would put me in front of regional officials.
Would that fix the next morning's demand?
No; the wildfire briefing remains fixed at 07:45.
I closed the week by updating the coordination room handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Should I take the Thursday evening command rehearsal when I am scheduled to brief the wildfire coordination group Friday at 07:45?
